description: AsyncTaskManager capacity and cancellation — cross-language golden test. Locks sync findings A-D-003 (submitting beyond max_tasks MUST raise the typed TASK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED error, not a generic error) and A-D-004 (cancelling a task while it is in retry backoff MUST stop further retry attempts and end in CANCELLED — expressed as a deterministic invariant on attempt count + final status, NOT a latency/timing assertion). Driver contract per case action below.

test_cases.notes: Driver: build AsyncTaskManager(max_tasks=1). Submit a first long-running task to occupy the slot, then submit a second; the second submit MUST raise the typed error whose code == TASK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (catchable by type, not a bare Error/RuntimeError).

Driver: submit a module that always fails (to trigger retry) with a per-attempt counter observable to the test. After the first failure, while the task is in its backoff wait, call cancel(taskId). Assert: (1) final task status == cancelled; (2) the module body's attempt counter does NOT increase after the cancel (no further retry attempt was started). This is the deterministic, non-timing form of the A-D-004 fix (TS previously waited out the full backoff before honoring cancel).
